name: returns
comment: Product returns and exchanges across all sales channels. One row per return. Every return carries its own channel_code directly (returns are not D2C-only) — use this column, not the original order's channel, when reporting returns by channel.

columns.name: hash_key
columns.comment: Deterministic hash of this record's natural/business key, generated during ingestion. Used internally for deduplication and change-detection; not a business attribute and should not be used for reporting.

columns.name: channel_code
columns.comment: Sales channel the ORIGINAL order (being returned) was placed on. Present for every return regardless of channel — do not assume returns exist only for D2C.

columns.name: original_order_ref
columns.comment: Reference to the original order/invoice being returned (matches the originating channel table's own order/invoice reference, e.g. order_name, invoice_no, order_id).

columns.name: exchange_order_ref
columns.comment: Reference to the new order created if this return was an exchange rather than a refund; NULL for a pure refund.

columns.name: return_type
columns.comment: Type of return (e.g. Refund, Exchange, Store Credit).

columns.name: reason_code
columns.comment: Reason the customer gave for the return (e.g. Damaged, Wrong Size, Changed Mind).

columns.name: initiated_at
columns.comment: Timestamp the customer initiated the return.

columns.name: warehouse_received_at
columns.comment: Timestamp the returned item was physically received back at the warehouse/store.

columns.name: refund_amount
columns.comment: Amount refunded to the customer for this return, in INR.

columns.name: restock_status
columns.comment: Whether the returned item was restockable (e.g. Restocked, Written Off, Pending Inspection).

columns.name: rn
columns.comment: Row number assigned per natural key by the ingestion pipeline (partitioned by business key, ordered by recency). rn = 1 identifies the current/latest version of a record when historized duplicates exist in this table.

columns.name: insert_timestamp
columns.comment: UTC timestamp when this record was first loaded into the silver layer. Reflects pipeline load time, not a business event time.

columns.name: modified_timestamp
columns.comment: UTC timestamp when this record was last updated by the ingestion pipeline. Reflects pipeline processing time, not a business event time.

columns.name: source_name
columns.comment: Name of the upstream source system or source file this record was ingested from. Used for data lineage and troubleshooting, not for business analysis.

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.comment: Soft-delete flag set by the ingestion pipeline when the source record was removed or tombstoned upstream. Rows where this is TRUE should normally be excluded from business reporting.

columns.name: return_date_key
columns.comment: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) the return was initiated, derived from initiated_at. Use this column to join to dim_date for month/quarter/year reporting on returns.
